NVDA.rationale: Nvidia exhibits exceptional fundamental health and trajectory: Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY, +43% QoQ) with EPS of $2.39 (+215% YoY), 75% gross margins, $50.3B operating cash flow in a single quarter, and a fortress balance sheet ($195B equity vs $8.5B debt, D/E of 0.043). Data center revenue of $75.2B (+92% YoY) represents ~92% of total revenue, with networking revenue surging 199% YoY. Q2 guidance of ~$91B signals no deceleration. The company's competitive position is dominant with ~85-92% market share in AI data center GPUs, CUDA ecosystem lock-in, and expanding into CPUs (Vera platform) and networking (now #1 in data center Ethernet switching per IDC). Valuation is attractive vs own history: P/E of 29.9x sits at the absolute bottom of its 365-day range (29.9-66.8), having compressed from ~53x in April 2026 as earnings surged. P/B of 24.4x is also at the floor of its 24.4-57.8 range. This represents a significant re-rating from the 50-57x P/E range that prevailed for most of the past year, driven by explosive earnings growth rather than price decline. The stock at $195.74 is up only 9.5% over the past quarter despite the massive earnings beat, suggesting the market has not fully repriced the earnings acceleration. Near-term catalysts include the June 24 shareholder meeting (with potential commentary on Vera Rubin ramp and $1T revenue visibility), Micron's blowout Q3 results (confirming robust AI memory demand that validates Nvidia's ecosystem), and the upcoming Q2 FY2027 earnings in late August with consensus expecting $91.7B revenue. Risks include China export control compliance scrutiny (Senator Warren probe), hyperscaler custom chip development (Amazon Trainium, Google TPU), and customer concentration (65% from four customers). However, these are well-known and the valuation already reflects significant skepticism at <30x P/E for a company growing 85%+ YoY.
